title: Past flight dates gave small and uncertain gains in British butterfly index forecasts in 2005-2024
abstract: We tested whether past flight timing adds information about next-year butterfly abundance beyond two years of population history. We used public UK Butterfly Monitoring Scheme 2024 records. Models fitted through 2004 forecast 2005-2024 at selected established British sites. Adding prior-year first, mean and last flight dates reduced equal-species mean squared log-index error by 0.83% across 29 species and 25,510 test triples. A three-year test-block range was 0.23% to 1.42%, conditional on fixed fits. The 2015-2024 gain for 27 species after fitting 1995-2014 was 0.47%, with range -0.07% to 1.06%. Both full-model ranges crossed zero when training-block weights also varied. At sites with complete test coverage, point gains were -0.35% and -0.54%, with wide ranges. That check selects persistent recorded populations and does not prove a site-turnover cause. Half of the timing-model addition retained small positive training-weight sensitivity ranges. Thus measured timing may carry a small signal, but these data do not establish a robust general gain. These tests overlap and reuse one monitoring system. Whole-season dates mix broods. Selected sites, shared count errors, final-release inputs and short test periods limit inference. Code, exact source hashes, aggregate errors, numerical checks and figures are included. External records and joined databases remain outside the baseline bundle.

display.caption: Past flight dates gave small forecast gains beyond two past annual indices. Ranges resample three-year test blocks with fixed model fits. The two test periods overlap.
Three-date forecast gains varied among selected butterfly species. Points are species scores at each split. They are not causal timing effects.

The full three-date gain was uncertain when training weights varied. The fixed-site subset gave negative point gains with wide ranges. The last row is a sensitivity distribution, not a calibrated confidence interval. All other ranges hold model fits fixed.
